Privatize

/PRY-vuh-tize/ - rhymes with size · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Privatize means to transfer from government to private ownership.

The kingdom privatized its postal service in stages, selling the parcel routes first.

Worked Example

For sixty winters the town ran its own skating rink at a cheerful loss — dollar skates, cocoa at cost, hours set at the annual meeting. Last March the council sold it, ice plant and all, to a family recreation company. The rink still opens at four; what changed is the deed. Season-pass prices now answer to the buyers' ledger, and the annual meeting votes on nothing colder than sidewalks.

Privatize is the exact word for that sale, because privatize means to transfer from government to private ownership — the deed moved, not just the work. Had the town merely hired the company to run its rink, that would be outsourcing, with the public still owner and the council still boss. Privatizing hands over the thing itself.

How Privatize Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

sell off

sell off: the plain phrase for the same transfer

denationalize

denationalize: the technical twin — undo state ownership

Antonyms

nationalize

nationalize: the state takes the deed the other way

collectivize

collectivize: fold it into shared public ownership

How Strong Is It? — subcontract → outsource → privatize

subcontract vs. privatize

subcontract vs. privatize: Subcontract hands over the least — one job, one contract, and the public owner still runs the show.

outsource vs. privatize

outsource vs. privatize: Outsource stops short of privatize — an outsourced service is run by a private firm while the public keeps the deed; privatizing sells the thing itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — privat

Root — privat: one's own, personal (Latin privus, privatus)

Suffix — -ize

Suffix — -ize: to make, to cause to be

Put it together

Put it together: Privat- (one's own) + -ize (to make) = to make something someone's own. Latin privus meant belonging to one person; privatus was what had been withdrawn from public life. Privatizing runs that withdrawal on paper: what the public owned becomes somebody's own.

Use the root in a new word: privilege

Use the root in a new word: privilege: Privilege joins privus to lex, law — originally a law passed for one person alone, which is why a privilege still belongs to the few.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / policy

Privatize is policy vocabulary, and its test is the deed: only when ownership itself crosses from state to private hands is the word earned. Outsource keeps the deed public and hires out the work; deregulate loosens the rules and moves nothing; nationalize is the same journey in reverse. Editorials load the word with cheers or alarm, but the mechanism it names is neutral paperwork.
